Subject: POC next steps: PulseAI trial plan, success criteria & capacity ask

Hi Emma / Liam —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and the recommended trial plan so we can get you running next week. Please confirm or flag anything missing.

Summary of what we heard
- Primary workload: real-time summarization + short-form generation for support triage (avg seq 128 / peak 512).
- Success criteria: 95th-pct latency < 220ms for single-request flows under target concurrency; 99% availability during business hours; intent detection F1 >= 0.88 on the provided eval set; cost target <= $0.06 per 1k tokens after batching and KV caching.

Proposed POC (4-week runbook)
1) Week 0 (onboarding): signed SOW, SOC2 evidence request (we've attached SOW draft), private seat + sandbox dataset ingest.
2) Week 1 (baseline): baseline eval on your eval set; smoke tests at production traffic profile.
3) Week 2 (tuning): apply quantization and batching recommendations; tune prompt templates; run A/B on model variants.
4) Week 3 (stress): 2-hour burst windows to validate autoscale & fallback.
5) Week 4 (handoff): final metrics, cost report, and rollout recommendation.

Capacity ask (initial reservation + burst policy)
- Reserved baseline: 4 x A100-style GPUs (multi-tenant dedicated pool) to meet sustained concurrency of 40 r/s with low-latency knobs.
- Autoscale burst policy: allow spikes up to 8 x GPUs for up to 3 hours/day (automatic scale based on policy) with graceful fallback to a quantized model if further capacity constrained.
- KV/prefix caching: we'll enable prefix caching for repeated dialogs which we estimate reduces token cost by ~18%.

Owners & next steps
- Action: Pulse to confirm success criteria and any additional STO (security/retention) asks — Owner: Emma (by EOD Thu).
- Action: Redwood to provide final SOW + capacity worksheet — Owner: Ben (by Tue 6/6).
- Action: Ops to reserve baseline pool after SOW — Owner: Neha (pending Ben).

Attachments: PulseAI_POC_SOW_v1.pdf, capacity_estimate_pulse.xlsx
Drive: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/pulseai/poc-plan

If that looks right I’ll loop in Neha to start reservations once we have a signed SOW.

Thanks,

Hi Emma, thanks for the questions — answering inline below.

> 1) SOC2 / retention: 
We can provide the SOC2 Type II packet (attached link) and our standard data retention options. For the POC we recommend a 30-day retention with automatic PII redaction on traces; we can enable stricter retention on request. Ben has attached a short checklist of evidence.

> 2) Autoscale & microbursts: 
Autoscale is reactive and we typically see warm-up latencies for adding GPUs ~2–6 minutes depending on region. For microbursts to 60 r/s, the safe path is baseline=6 GPUs with aggressive prefix caching + continuous batching to shave per-token time. Alternatively, we can configure a warm standby (1–2 hot instances) that keeps capacity immediately available at a slightly higher hourly cost. My recommendation: start at baseline=6, configure burst up to 8 for 3 hours/day, and enable warm standby threads for 1 hour/day during peak windows on weekdays.

Estimated cost delta (very rough)
- Baseline 4 -> 6 GPUs: +~$7,200/month (depends on region & SKU).
- Warm standby addition: +~$1,400/month for 1-2 hot instances during peak windows.
We'll produce a line-item estimate in the attached capacity_estimate_pulse.xlsx.

> 3) Median tokens:
Great — please share sample prompts. We’ll run a short prompt-optimization sprint during Week 1 to hit the median token target.

Next steps I’ll own: finalize SOW with a 6 baseline option included; attach SOC2 packet to the SOW email thread. Neha — can you provision the tentative 6-GPU pool once we get a signed SOW?

Thanks,
